topic.title: Shared generated-file proposal and diff contract for React parity
topic.prompt: Should NeuroCLI define a shared generated-file proposal and diff contract so the React frontend can review AI file updates before apply while preserving the Textual review flow?

project_context.overview: NeuroCLI has one shared Python backend workflow in neurocli_core, a Textual frontend in neurocli_app, a FastAPI bridge in api, and a React frontend in web_client.
project_context.current_phase: Phase 5 frontend polish and feature parity, with generated-file review called out as the main parity gap.
architectural_constraints: neurocli_core remains the backend source of truth.
api is a bridge to neurocli_core rather than a second behavior layer.
React must not invent backend workflow logic in web_client.
Gemini owns React presentation work only; Codex owns contracts and integration logic.

files_or_sources_reviewed.relevance: Defines Codex and Gemini ownership boundaries and the one-backend/two-frontends architecture.
Identifies generated-file review as the current React parity gap.
Records shared workflow contract fields and current frontend/backend constraints.
States that React should not fake generated-file diff review without a Codex-defined contract.

participating_agents.perspective: Protect shared backend contracts and prevent duplicated workflow logic.
responsibilities: Protect neurocli_core as source of truth
non_goals: Implement runtime changes inside a planning artifact

participating_agents.perspective: Keep the developer review loop clear, inspectable, and consistent across surfaces.
non_goals: Prioritize polish over a real data path

participating_agents.perspective: Ensure generated model output is structured enough to audit and apply safely.
non_goals: Assume free-form output can be applied safely

participating_agents.perspective: Challenge claims, missing tests, and unverified parity assumptions.
non_goals: Treat sample output as a real council run

participating_agents.perspective: Sequence work into small, verifiable phases with clear owners.
responsibilities: Separate contract, integration, and presentation work
non_goals: Start with Gemini UI changes before contract work

participating_agents.perspective: Keep Textual and React capabilities aligned without forcing identical presentation.
responsibilities: Protect ownership between Codex and Gemini
non_goals: Treat presentation parity as contract parity

conversation_rounds.summary: The council independently proposed a shared proposal/diff object as the safest way to close the React review gap.

agent_contributions.position: Add a shared generated-file proposal contract in neurocli_core and expose it through api before React UI work.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: No change yet; the first position is contract-first.

agent_contributions.position: Improve the user review loop so React users can inspect generated file changes before apply.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: No change yet; the proposal focuses on review clarity.

agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: No change yet; the proposal centers on auditable output.

agent_contributions.position: Protect against declaring parity without tests for missing targets, malformed model output, and apply failures.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: No change yet; QA requires explicit verification.

agent_contributions.position: Phase the work as contract design, backend tests, API bridge, React integration, and Gemini presentation polish.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: No change yet; sequencing starts with Codex-owned logic.

agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: No change yet; parity means capability alignment.

conversation_rounds.name: Critique and Challenge
conversation_rounds.summary: The council challenged UI-first approaches, vague diff semantics, and insufficient validation.

agent_contributions.position: A React-only diff would violate the backend source-of-truth rule.
challenges_received: Product/UX asked whether contract work delays user-visible parity.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: Accepted that the contract should be minimal and focused on the existing review loop.

agent_contributions.position: The contract must still support a clean user story: generate, review, edit if needed, apply with backup.
challenges_received: Skeptic/QA questioned whether edit behavior creates additional testing scope.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: Separated required generated diff review from optional advanced editor behavior.

agent_contributions.position: Free-form `output_text` should not be the only applyable artifact for generated file updates.
challenges_received: Implementation Planner asked for a smaller first contract.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: Reduced the first contract to target path, proposed content, normalized content, diff text, and status.

agent_contributions.position: Tests must cover malformed AI responses and files outside the workspace.
challenges_received: Architecture Guardian noted workspace path checks already exist in api.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: Kept path tests but scoped them to the new proposal endpoint or response fields.

agent_contributions.position: Gemini should wait for the bridge shape before final presentation polish.
challenges_received: Frontend Parity Advocate asked whether existing ReviewModal can still be used.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: Allowed React to reuse existing presentation state after Codex updates the data source.

agent_contributions.position: The user-facing gap is not just a modal; it is the absence of the same generated diff confidence Textual has.
challenges_received: Product/UX asked whether identical UI is necessary.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: Clarified that identical UI is not required; equivalent review capability is required.

decisions: Do not solve generated-file diff review as a frontend-only feature.

conversation_rounds.name: Reconciliation and Prioritization
conversation_rounds.summary: The council reconciled around a minimal shared proposal contract, with UI polish explicitly deferred until after Codex-owned integration work.

agent_contributions.position: Contract design belongs in neurocli_core with api exposing the same semantics to React.
challenges_received: Implementation Planner asked whether Textual must change immediately.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: Textual can be adapted after the contract is proven, without removing its current review path first.

agent_contributions.position: The first usable milestone is visible diff review in React, not a full editor suite.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: Added exit criteria around diff visibility, disabled apply on invalid proposal, and error recovery.

agent_contributions.position: Proposal status should distinguish generated content, formatted content, diff creation failure, and non-file chat output.
challenges_received: Architecture Guardian warned against over-expanding the first schema.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: Kept status explicit but deferred richer metadata until after first tests.

agent_contributions.position: Unit tests should pin the normalized proposal shape before browser work is claimed complete.
challenges_received: Product/UX asked for manual verification too.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: Added browser smoke testing after unit and API tests.

agent_contributions.position: Codex should implement contract and integration, then Gemini can refine presentation in web_client.
challenges_received: Frontend Parity Advocate requested a shared decision update.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: Added `handoff/coordination/shared_decisions.md` as an explicit documentation update.

agent_contributions.position: React parity is complete only when the review path consumes backend-generated proposal data.
challenges_received: Skeptic/QA asked how to detect regression.
agent_contributions.changes_after_challenge: Added parity checks comparing Textual and React generated-file workflows.

decisions: Prioritize a minimal contract, backend/API tests, React integration, then presentation polish.

major_disagreements.topic: Whether React can close the gap with UI-only diff handling.

positions.claim: A fast UI improvement could make the review loop feel better sooner.
positions.rationale: Users experience the gap in React, so visible review matters.

positions.claim: UI-only diff handling would create duplicated workflow behavior.
positions.rationale: The repo explicitly requires backend workflow behavior to stay in neurocli_core.

major_disagreements.topic: How rich the first proposal contract should be.

positions.claim: The contract should include enough status metadata to make AI output auditable.
positions.rationale: Generated file content can fail formatting, diffing, or target validation.

positions.claim: The first pass should stay minimal to avoid blocking Phase 5 on schema design.
positions.rationale: A small contract can be tested and expanded after it proves useful.

resolved_recommendations.title: Define a shared generated-file proposal contract
resolved_recommendations.decision: Create a minimal contract in neurocli_core that represents target path, proposed content, normalized content, diff text, proposal status, and errors.
resolved_recommendations.rationale: React cannot safely match Textual generated-file review while it treats output_text as directly applyable content.
dependencies: Tests for proposal generation and failure states

resolved_recommendations.title: Expose the proposal contract through the FastAPI bridge
resolved_recommendations.decision: Have api return the same proposal semantics to React that Textual can consume directly from neurocli_core.
resolved_recommendations.rationale: The bridge should expose shared backend behavior instead of creating a separate interpretation layer.

resolved_recommendations.title: Let Gemini polish presentation after contract integration
resolved_recommendations.decision: Gemini can refine React review UI once Codex wires real proposal data into React state.
resolved_recommendations.rationale: This preserves ownership boundaries and avoids UI that implies unsupported backend behavior.

unresolved_questions.question: Should Textual immediately migrate to the new proposal object or keep its current review implementation until React parity is proven?
unresolved_questions.why_it_matters: A forced migration could create unnecessary risk in the strongest current review path.

unresolved_questions.question: Should AI commit-message generation become a shared contract in the same Phase 5 slice?
unresolved_questions.why_it_matters: It is another parity gap, but bundling it with generated-file review may broaden the work too much.

risks.risk: React presents a diff that was not produced by the shared backend workflow.
risks.mitigation: Require backend proposal data before declaring React generated-file parity complete.
risks.detection_signal: web_client computes generated-file review state without a matching api or neurocli_core field.

risks.risk: The proposal contract becomes too broad and delays the parity fix.
risks.mitigation: Start with a minimal required field set and defer advanced editor metadata.
risks.detection_signal: Schema discussion expands into unrelated git, radar, or command-palette features.

risks.risk: Tests cover only successful generation and miss malformed AI output.
risks.mitigation: Add failure-state tests for missing target files, formatting errors, and invalid generated content.
risks.detection_signal: Only happy-path tests exist for proposal generation.

frontend_implications: React should consume backend proposal data before Gemini treats review presentation as complete.
Textual should keep its review flow stable while the shared contract is introduced.
backend_implications: neurocli_core needs to own proposal semantics if the recommendation becomes implementation work.
api needs to expose the same semantics without interpreting generated content separately.

contract_considerations.details: A future implementation would require Codex to define or approve a shared generated-file proposal contract before React presentation work proceeds.

testing_considerations.recommendation: Add unit tests for proposal creation, formatting success, formatting failure, and non-file chat output.
Add tests that confirm the FastAPI bridge returns proposal fields without allowing paths outside the workspace.
Run a browser smoke test showing generated proposal review, disabled invalid apply, edit, and apply-with-backup behavior.

suggested_implementation_phases.goal: Define the minimal proposal object in neurocli_core and document it in shared decisions.
Expose proposal data through api and add backend/API tests.
Wire React integration state to backend proposal data without changing presentation ownership.
exit_criteria: React no longer treats raw output_text as the only generated-file proposal source

suggested_implementation_phases.goal: Polish React review presentation after the real data path exists.
exit_criteria: Review UI displays backend proposal state
Wide and narrow browser layouts are checked
No frontend-only backend behavior is introduced

final_synthesis_summary: This sample council recommends treating React generated-file review as a contract-first Phase 5 parity item. The next implementation should be Codex-owned: define minimal proposal semantics in neurocli_core, expose them through api, test failure states, then let React consume the real data before Gemini polishes presentation.
